sentences.text: Hello, everyone, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I'm Emily, your host.
Today, we are traveling to a beautiful and traditional city
in Japan, Kyoto.
Kyoto is full of temples, gardens, and peaceful streets.
It is one of the most loved cities in Japan.
Let's explore the calm and beauty of Kyoto together.
Part 2. Where is Kyoto?
Kyoto is in the center of Japan on the island of Hanshu.
It used to be the capital city of Japan for more than 1,000 years.
Today, it is smaller than Tokyo, but full of culture and history.
You can reach Kyoto by train in about two and a half hours from Tokyo.
Part 3. A short history.
Kyoto was founded in the year 794.
It was Japan's capital and the home of the emperor for many centuries.
During that time, many temples, palaces, and gardens were built.
Even today, Kyoto keeps its old charm and traditions alive.
It is now a UNESCO World Heritage City and one of the most visited places in Japan.
Part 4. What does Kyoto look like?
Kyoto is a mix of the old and the new.
There are quiet streets with wooden houses and small shops.
You can see mountains around the city and rivers crossing through.
In spring, cherry blossoms make the whole city pink and beautiful.
In autumn, the trees turn red, orange, and gold.
It's like living inside a painting.
Part 5. The people of Kyoto.
People in Kyoto are polite, calm, and respectful.
They care deeply about traditions and beauty.
They like to walk quietly, speak gently, and bow when greeting others.
Hospitality is very important.
Visitors are treated with kindness.
You'll hear many people saying arigato gozaimasu, which means thank you very much.
Part 6. Food in Kyoto.
Food in Kyoto is light, beautiful, and full of flavor.
One famous meal is kaiseiki, a traditional multi-course dinner.
It includes soup, rice, fish, and small dishes made from seasonal ingredients.
People also enjoy matcha, a green tea powder used in tea ceremonies.
Kyoto is famous for its sweets made with matcha.
They look like little pieces of art.
Part 7. Temples and shrines.
Kyoto has more than 1,600 temples and 400 shrines.
Some of the most famous ones are kinkakuji, the golden pavilion covered in gold leaf, fushimi
anari shrine, with its thousands of red gates, kiyomi zudara, a temple with amazing views
of the city.
These places are peaceful and full of history.
Part 8. Nature around Kyoto.
Kyoto is surrounded by green hills and forests.
You can visit arashiyama, a beautiful area with bamboo forests.
Walking through the tall bamboo feels magical and quiet.
There is also a river where people take boat rides and relax.
Nature in Kyoto is always close.
Even in the middle of the city.
Part 9. Culture and Art.
Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture.
It is the home of geisha, traditional female artists who dance and play music.
You can see them in the Jion district, wearing beautiful kimonos.
Kyoto is also famous for tea ceremonies, calligraphy and flower arranging.
All about balance and beauty.
Part 10. Festivals in Kyoto.
There are many festivals in Kyoto during the year.
One of the biggest is Jion Matsuri in July.
It has big parades, music and traditional clothes.
In spring, people celebrate Hanami when cherry blossoms bloom.
Families and friends sit under trees to enjoy the flowers and eat together.
Part 11. Daily Life in Kyoto.
Life in Kyoto is calm and organized.
People wake up early, go to work or school and often use bicycles or trains.
In the evening they might visit a shrine or enjoy quiet tea with friends.
The city has many small shops, traditional houses and peaceful streets.
It's a perfect place for people who love beauty and simplicity.
Part 12. Goodbye from Kyoto.
Thank you for joining me on this journey to Kyoto, Japan.
It's a city where old traditions meet modern life.
From temples to bamboo forests, Kyoto shows the quiet heart of Japan.
If you want peace, beauty and culture, Kyoto is waiting for you.
Goodbye, or as people in Japan say, Sayonara.
